summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony: analyze confidential supply-chain data drops, find hidden launch risks (Collector's Edition shortfalls), and build a general, adaptable agent product that rechecks the plan on each new drop and takes real supplier actions with human approval.
summary.outcome: Found that the plan says 'ok' while art books, statues, game cards and packing speed break the Collector's Edition. Built the ask_soony app with a poller, versioned store, verifier, papercheck, a Today decision UI, routines, a sent-mailbox sync with duplicate-send guard, and drop-drill fixes. Sent the Karton art-book order and the supplier reply, and redesigned the routine diagram. Hand-in materials (README, demo script, video), a push, and the confirmed-order-as-inbound feature were still pending.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks. Change detection must poll and compare per-file SHA-256, because files are replaced under the same name and formats can change.
Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored data/ folder; .env holds the token, and .env.example is committed with an empty token.

The team shares one mailbox, so emails sent by hand or by teammate code (Lucas's Pulse console on origin/new-approach) are invisible to the app. The app now reads the sent folder and blocks duplicate sends within 12h unless 'Send anyway' is used (409 otherwise, also for voice and routines).
Teammates' workflow files CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md exist; claim tasks in PROGRESS.md before building.

Drop-drill findings: renamed CSV columns silently auto-closed real cards, a news drop crashed the pipeline because two modules wrote the same impacts file, tracker version ordering picked the oldest file, and any address in a supplier JSON profile was trusted as a send target. All were fixed.
Entire hooks only write a checkpoint when repo files change; sessions with no file changes log 'skipping checkpoint'.
A reply to a side email (e.g. tracking questions) must not mark a case as sent or decided; it only adds information.

code.finding: New module syncing the shared mailbox's sent folder. It assigns mails to cases by thread reference, then supplier plus PO, then a unique part number, and feeds the duplicate-send guard.

Compares newer JSON supplier profiles with profile.csv and raises status or qualification cards. New contact emails are not used as send targets until confirmed. Commit b0cff82 initially imported it before it was committed, which broke HEAD.

Routine diagram rewritten into n8n-style nodes: a When node, one 'Only if' node with a numbered checklist and funnel counts, and one Then node per step. Arrows run only between groups because the conditions are an AND list.
Browser-side funnel counts and near-duplicate condition detection mirror routines.py logic, so they can drift from the server and are approximate for waiting and replies triggers.

workflow: Use subagents for large cross-checks (200 order confirmations plus 59 scans) and for UX review, but verify their commits: a builder's uncommitted edits were swept into another commit.
Screenshot UI changes in a headless browser on a copy of state with background jobs off, then check them before committing.
Check the 'Needs you' queue, mailbox and portal for new drops regularly, since the portal gives no notifications.
Hackathon scoring rewards specific data-grounded questions plus general pain/product questions in office hours.

friction: The portal token was initially empty, which blocked data access until it was provided.
Shared mailbox caused a double art-book order (the app at 06:50 and by hand at 07:04), and Pulse sent confusing internal emails to Hwaseong with no recipient allow-list.
Commit b0cff82 accidentally included uncommitted api.py edits that imported an untracked module, so HEAD alone would not start.
Browser layout bugs: a button-based source link forced a stray period onto its own line, and the left case list neither expanded nor scrolled with J/K.
Scanned PDFs and non-English documents needed rendering and translation.
The app's sign-off rule is stricter than Soony's policy, sending every case with a cost to Maren instead of using approval limits.
open_items: Push 12+ commits on branch jonas/today-flow (awaiting user approval).
Commit the hybrid n8n-style routine diagram (FlowGraph.tsx and RoutineCard.tsx), which was verified but whose commit result isn't shown.
Finish the 'confirmed orders become inbound deliveries' builder: estimate Karton art-book arrival (~19:30) against the 11:16 cell stop and open a follow-up case if too late.
Combine the four 'Are there really…?' count questions into one case or raise their visibility threshold.
Send a note to Hwaseong disregarding the Pulse test emails, and message Lucas about the missing allow-list in Pulse.
Use approval limits from the policy (e.g. Paul Winter's 50k EUR) instead of routing every costed case to Maren.
Write the README, demo script and video for the 12:00 hand-in.

Memo rules (Quality & Compliance last word, air/rush to CPO within the hour) are extracted but not used for routing; the predictor was never run for real; a renamed stock column still reads as zero stock.
Ask the Lio engineers whether portal data is identical across teams and whether supplier actions create files; the Claude doc and briefing artifact still show the 14:00 state.
Register sender addresses in the portal settings, and decide whether to delete the earlier Claude doc.
